DepthShaded Maximum Intensity Projection (DSMIP) is a volume rendering technique that enhances depth perception in Maximum Intensity Projection (MIP) by modulating the final color based on the depth of the sampled structures [S1, unofficial][S3].

The claim states that DepthShaded Maximum Intensity Projection (DSMIP) enhances depth perception in MIP by modulating final color based on depth. Source [S3] explicitly describes a technique called DEMIP (Depth-enhanced Maximum Intensity Projection) which calculates the final color by blending the MIP color with a depth-derived color using a specific formula involving a depth weight and normalized depth value. This directly supports the mechanism described in the claim. Source [S1] also describes DeMIP as modifying MIP shading based on the depth of closer structures to enhance depth perception. Although the claim uses the acronym 'DSMIP' while the sources use 'DeMIP' or 'DEMIP', the description of the technique (modulating color based on depth to enhance perception) is fully supported by the evidence provided in both sources.

A method to improve depth perception in MIP by extracting isosurfaces and modifying vertex coordinates before projection [S1, unofficial].
